Rashi on Yevamot 47a:10:1.hebrew: ואין עדות לעובד כוכבים - הואיל ובניך מוחזקין בכשרות, אין אתה נאמן להעיד עליהן ולפוסלן:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:10:1.english: And there is no testimony for an idolater - Since your children are presumed [to be] fit, you are not deemed credible to testify about them and render them unfit.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:10:2.hebrew: לפסול את בניך - דנפקא לן מיכיר, ואי אתה נאמן לפסול את בני בניך:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:10:2.english: To render your children unfit - For we derive [this] from [the verse] "he shall acknowledge," and you are not deemed credible to render your grandchildren unfit.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:1.hebrew: והלכתא כרב נחמן - דאמר לדבריו עובד כוכבים הוא, ואין עדות לעובד כוכבים, ואפילו אבנים לא מהימן:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:1.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rav Nachman - Who said [that] according to his [own] words he is a gentile, and a gentile has no [valid] testimony, and even regarding [his] sons he is not believed.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:2.hebrew: והתניא כרבינא - דנאמן הוא על בנו קטן שאין לו בנים, וקס"ד דהא מתני' בגר שבא ואמר גר אני קמיירי:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:2.english: But isn't it taught [in a baraita] in accordance with Ravina - That he is believed regarding his minor son who has no children, and we initially thought that this baraita is speaking of a convert who came and said, "I am a convert."

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:3.english: That [baraita] - which teaches [that] he is believed regarding his minor son.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:4.hebrew: לענין יכיר - תניא אההיא מתני' דיכיר קאי, דקתני: וכשם שנאמן אדם לומר "זה בני בכור", כך נאמן לומר "זה בני בן גרושה"; ועלה קתני דנאמן הוא על הקטן, דהא ישראל הוא ויש לו עדות, והתורה האמינתו על בנו ולא על בן בנו. אבל גבי גר, אפילו אבנו לא מהימן, דאין עדות לעובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:12:4.english: Concerning "he shall acknowledge" - [That which] was taught [in the baraita] refers to that Mishnah of "he shall acknowledge," which teaches: "And just as a person is believed to say, 'This is my firstborn son,' so is he believed to say, 'This is my son, the son of a divorcée.'" And regarding it, [the baraita] teaches that he is believed concerning a minor [son], for he is a Jew and has [valid] testimony, and the Torah believed him regarding his son, but not regarding his son's son. However, regarding a convert, even concerning his son he is not believed, for a gentile has no [valid] testimony.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:13:1.hebrew: וסחופין - שפלים וכפויין, כמו סחופי כסא (שבת דף סו:), כפיית הכלי:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:13:1.english: And sechufin - Low and overturned, like sechufei kasa (Shabbat 66b), [meaning] the overturning of a vessel.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:13:2.hebrew: ואיני כדאי - ואיני ראוי להשתתף בצרתן, ומי יתן ואזכה לכך:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:13:2.english: And I am unworthy - And I am not worthy to share in their distress, and would that I merit this.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:14:1.hebrew: ומודיעים אותו - לקמן מפרש טעמא דכולה מתני':
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:14:1.english: And they inform him - Later, [the Gemara] explains the reason for the entire Mishnah.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:1:1.english: In any place that [he is] with you - And later on [the Gemara] asks: Haven't you already used it?

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:1:2.hebrew: צריך להביא ראיה - שבב"ד נתגייר, שמא גבעוני מהול הוא, ומשום שבחא דא"י הוא דקאמר הכי ומשקר:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:1:2.english: He needs to bring evidence - That he converted in a court, [for] perhaps he is a circumcised Gibeonite, and it is because of the excellence of the Land of Israel that he says this and is lying.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:2:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> מהו דתימא לא ניהמניהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:2:1.english: We read [the text as]: "What might you have said? We should not believe them."

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:3:1.english: From "with you" [immakh] - [From the verse:] "a stranger and a resident, that he may live with you" (Leviticus 25:35).

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:5:1.english: When there is no goodness - For milk and honey have ceased.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:6:1.hebrew: דקמסייעי קראי - דהא "עמך" כל מקום שאתך משמע, ואפילו בארץ, ו"בארצכם" למה לי? אלא לאו אראיה קאי, דבארץ צריך להביא ראיה ולא בחוצה לארץ:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:6:1.english: Because the verses support [him] - For "with you" implies anywhere that is with you, even in the Land [of Israel]; so why do I need "in your land"? Rather, does it not refer to [bringing] proof, that in the Land [of Israel] one must bring proof, and not outside the Land [of Israel]?

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:7:1.hebrew: מדכתיב "גר" אצל "ושפטתם", מכאן אמר <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> יהודה: גר בעי בית דין:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:7:1.english: Since "convert" is written alongside "and you shall judge," from here Rabbi Yehuda said: A convert requires a court.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:9:1.english: He shall acknowledge - the firstborn, the son of the hated [wife], he shall acknowledge.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:9:2.hebrew: יכירנו לאחרים - שאם אין ב"ד מכירים אותו, נאמן עליו אביו לומר "זה בני בכור" ליטול פי שנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 47a:9:2.english: He can identify him to others - [Meaning] that if the court does not recognize him, his father is deemed credible regarding him to say, "This is my firstborn son," to take a double portion.

Rashi on Yevamot 47a:9:3.english: He is a son of a divorced woman - And he is a ḥalal [disqualified] priest.

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:10:1.english: And there is no testimony for an idolater - [However,] regarding himself he is deemed credible, because he has rendered himself a forbidden piece [i.e., he has established a prohibited status upon himself].

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:10:2.hebrew: ואין אתה נאמן לפסול בני בניך - אומר ר"י דה"פ: "נאמן אתה לפסול בניך" — פי', כשאין לו אלא בנים ואין לו בני בנים; "ואי אתה נאמן לפסול בני בניך" — כשיש לו בני בנים, אין נאמן לפסול אפי' בניו, דאין סברא לומר שיהיו בניו פסולים ובני בניו כשרים. וכן משמע בסמוך, דקאמר: "ואין אדם נאמן על בנו גדול", ומפרש: "כשיש לו בנים", משמע דאבנו נמי לא מהימן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:10:2.english: And you are not deemed credible to render your grandchildren unfit - The Ri says that this is its explanation: "You are deemed credible to render your children unfit" — meaning, when he has only children and does not have grandchildren; "and you are not deemed credible to render your grandchildren unfit" — [meaning that] when he has grandchildren, he is not deemed credible to render even his children unfit, for it is not logical to say that his children are unfit while his grandchildren are fit. And so it is implied immediately below, where [the Gemara] says: "And a person is not deemed credible regarding his adult son," and explains: "when he has children," which implies that regarding his son as well he is not deemed credible.

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:12:1.hebrew: והלכתא כוותיה דרב נחמן בר יצחק - משמע דהלכה כר"י דנאמן אף לפסול בניו, דדוקא משום דאין עדות לעובד כוכבים דאין יכול לפוסלן; ולא כמו שמפרש רבינו תם, דאין הלכה כרבי יהודה אלא כשפוסל אחרים על ידי הכרת בכור, אבל בלא הכרת בכור — לא. ובשאלתות בפרשת וירא נמי דקדק מהך דשמעתין, דבכל ענין הלכה כרבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:12:1.english: And the halakha is in accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak - This implies that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, that [a father] is believed even to disqualify his sons, for it is specifically because a gentile has no [valid] testimony that he cannot disqualify them; and not as Rabbeinu Tam explains, that the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah except when he disqualifies others by means of acknowledging a firstborn, but without acknowledging a firstborn, [the halakha is] not [in accordance with him]. And in the She'iltot, in Parashat Vayera, he also inferred from this [passage] of our sugya that in all cases the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah.

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:1:1.hebrew: אין לי אלא בארץ - פי' דמקבלין גרים, ואע"ג דחובת הגוף היא — בעיא ריבויא כיון דכתיב "בארץ", כדאשכחן בסוף פ"ק דקידושין (דף לח:) גבי שילוח עבדים והשמטת כספים. אי נמי: בארץ לא חיישינן דלמא הדרי בהו, משום דאיכא שבחא דארץ ישראל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:1:1.english: I have [derived] only in the Land - [This] means that we accept converts [only in the Land]. And even though [conversion] is a personal obligation, it requires a [Scriptural] inclusion since "in the land" is written [in the verse], as we find at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin (38b) regarding the emancipation of slaves and the remission of debts. Alternatively: in the Land [of Israel] we are not concerned lest they retract [their conversion], because there is the advantage of the Land of Israel.

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:2:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא לא להימניהו - ויש ספרים דגרסי "מהו דתימא ליהמניהו", וה"פ: ליהמניהו כעד מפי עד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:2:1.english: What might you have said, [that] we should not believe them - And there are texts that read: "What might you have said, we should believe them?" — and this is its explanation: [Should] we believe them like a witness from the mouth of a witness?

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:8:1.hebrew: יש לך עדים - פירוש: שנתגיירת בינך לבין עצמך. ותימה מיהא: אי הא דבעינן ג' היינו דוקא לכתחלה, אבל דיעבד חד נמי כשר, א"כ אם יש לו עדים לאו בינו לבין עצמו הוא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:8:1.english: [Do] you have witnesses - Explanation: that you converted in private. However, this is puzzling: if [the rule] that we require three [judges] is only lekhatchilah [initially], whereas di'eved [after the fact] even one is valid, if so, if he has witnesses, it is not in private!

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:8:2.hebrew: נאמן אתה לפסול עצמך כו' - היינו דוקא במילי דמשוי נפשיה חתיכה דאיסורא, אבל אם בא על בת כהן לא פסלה, כדפרישית לעיל בסוף פ' שני (יבמות דף כה: ושם). וא"ת: היכי דמי? אם אשתו עובדת כוכבים — ממה נפשך בניו פסולים, דאין קרוי "בנך" אלא בנה; ואם היתה אשתו ישראלית — ממה נפשך בניו כשרים, דקי"ל (לעיל יבמות דף מה.): עובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל — הולד כשר. וכי תימא: נהי דממזר לא הוי, פגום מיהא הוי — הא השתא נמי דאין נאמן פגומין הם, דר"י אית ליה בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין עז.) דבת גר זכר כבת חלל זכר. וי"ל דקסבר ר"י: עובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל — הולד ממזר, דבפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נג. ושם) אמר דר' יהודה סבר לה כרבי עקיבא, דאמר אין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:8:2.english: You are deemed credible to render yourself unfit, etc. - This applies specifically in matters where he renders himself a forbidden entity [lit., a piece of prohibition], but if he cohabited with the daughter of a priest, he has not disqualified her [from eating terumah or marrying a priest], as I explained above at the end of the second chapter (Yevamot 25b, and there). And if you ask: What are the circumstances [of this case]? If his wife is an idolatress [i.e., a non-Jew], either way his children are unfit, for [the child] is not called "your son," rather "her son"; and if his wife was a Jewess, either way his children are fit, as we hold as an established law (above, Yevamot 45a) [that when] a non-Jew or a slave cohabits with a Jewish woman, the offspring is fit. And if you should say: Granted that [the child] is not a mamzer, he is nevertheless genealogically tainted [if the father is a non-Jew] — [that cannot be,] for even now, when he is not deemed credible [and is presumed to be a convert], they are [already] tainted, since Rabbi Yehuda holds in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 77a) that the daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male chalal [and is disqualified from marrying a priest]. And one can answer that Rabbi Yehuda holds [that when] a non-Jew or a slave cohabits with a Jewish woman, the offspring is a mamzer; for in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 53a, and there) it states that Rabbi Yehuda concurs with Rabbi Akiva, who says that betrothal does not take effect in [relationships prohibited by] negative commandments:

Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:9:1.hebrew: כך נאמן אדם לומר זה בן גרושה - ר' אליהו מפרי"ש מפרש דנפקא לן מדכתיב "בן השנואה יכיר" (דברים כ״א:י״ז), וכן משמע בירושלמי בפרק בתרא דקידושין. ולשון הש"ס לא משמע הכי, דקתני "כשם שנאמן אדם לומר זה בני בכור" — משמע דמינה גמר. וי"מ דטעמא דר' יהודה דמשמע ליה קרא דנאמן אדם לומר "זה בני בכור" אפי' על תינוק בין הבנים; וכשאומר על הקטן שהוא בכור, א"כ הראשון ממזר — אלמא דנאמן לפוסלו, וה"נ דנאמן לומר שהוא בן גרושה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 47a:9:1.english: So [too] is a man deemed credible to say: This is a son of a divorced woman - Rabbi Eliyahu of Paris explains that we derive [this] from that which is written: "the son of the hated [wife] he shall acknowledge" (Deuteronomy 21:17), and so it is implied in the Jerusalem Talmud in the last chapter of Kiddushin. However, the language of the Talmud does not imply this, as it teaches: "Just as a man is deemed credible to say: This is my firstborn son" — implying that it derives [this] from that [clause itself]. And some explain that Rabbi Yehuda's reason is that the verse implies to him that a man is deemed credible to say "This is my firstborn son" even regarding a child among [his] sons; and when he says regarding the younger one that he is the firstborn, if so, the first [son] is a mamzer — thus [we see] that he is deemed credible to disqualify him, and so too here he is deemed credible to say that he is the son of a divorced woman.
